subject: MAP: POC onramp — org seed, API keys, allowlist & VPC peering
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@cardiosense.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP: POC onramp — org seed, API keys, allowlist & VPC peering

Evan — great to connect yesterday. Per our mutual action plan I pulled together the minimal onboarding sequence so your infra team can stage the POC this week. High level asks and owners below: 

- Org & tenant creation: CardioSense should create the Redwoods tenant name you want us to seed (recommended: cardiosense-prodtest) — owner: CardioSense infra (Aisha).
- API key seeding: we'll generate scoped API keys tied to the tenant. For the POC please request two keys (ingest + eval) and mark expiry for 30 days. We will provide the exact 'role' mapping.
- IP allowlist: provide CIDR ranges for both your test infra and any NAT egress. We will add to our allowlist for the tenant.
- VPC peering: provide the VPC ID, region, and a preferred peering window (we can do quick peering Tues–Thu, 8–18 PDT). We'll coordinate route tables.

Deliverables from us by EOD today: updated MAP spreadsheet (attached), sample API scope JSON, and a one-page network sketch for peering (attached). Can you confirm owners and the CIDRs + preferred peering window? Also copying Ben and Neha from our infra and security teams for the peering and allowlist steps.

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0192

Attachments: MAP-CardioSense-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), poes_network_sketch.pdf (diagram)

From: Evan Liu <evan.liu@cardiosense.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Verma <aisha.verma@cardiosense.ai>, security@cardiosense.ai
Date: 2026-09-23T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: POC onramp — org seed, API keys, allowlist & VPC peering

Thanks Olga — this is helpful. Quick answers from our side: 

- Owner: Aisha will take tenant creation. We will call it cardiosense-poc-1.
- CIDRs: our staging NAT egress is 35.182.10.0/24; test runners are behind 10.18.0.0/16 (we can add a small public egress range if you need outbound rules).
- VPC: VPC-0a1b2c (us-west-2). Preferred peering window: Tues 2026-09-28 09:00–11:00 PDT.

Security flagged one ask: we need the exact API key scope and storage retention for logs tied to the eval run. I copied security@cardiosense.ai (team inbox) — they may request a brief SOC2 scoping note. Also Ben — can you propose minimal RBAC for the API key roles?

On the MAP spreadsheet: can you add a short column for acceptance criteria per step so we can sign off quickly?

—Evan

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@cardiosense.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-23T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: POC onramp — org seed, API keys, allowlist & VPC peering

Evan/Aisha — thanks for the details. Quick notes from infra/security: 

- API key scopes: we will provide two scoped key templates today: "poc-ingest" (token creation + ingest-only) and "poc-eval" (read-only outputs + metric hooks). Both keys will be bound to the tenant cardiosense-poc-1 and limited to your allowlisted IPs.
- Retention & logs: for the POC we keep request logs for 30 days by default; if CardioSense needs longer retention we can discuss a short add-on. We'll document what fields are stored in the SOC2 scoping note.
- RBAC: minimal RBAC for the two keys: poc-ingest -> service principal; poc-eval -> CI user. We will also create a read-only admin view in console for Aisha so she can rotate keys.
- Peering checklist: please confirm the peering CIDR for the VPC (we have the VPC ID but need the exact subnet to avoid overlap). We'll perform asymmetric route validation in the window Evan suggested (2026-09-28 09:00–11:00 PDT).

I attached a short peering runbook (inline in the network PDF) and added an acceptance-criteria column to the MAP spreadsheet (see attachment). Proposed next steps: 
1) CardioSense (Aisha) confirms subnets + signs the acceptance cell for "VPC peering scheduled".
2) Redwood (Ben/Neha) creates the two keys and posts them into the MAP secure notes.
3) Post-peering: run a smoke test (generate 50 short requests) and capture latency & error rates for acceptance.

If that works I will generate the keys and post a DocuSign-style acknowledgement in the MAP so legal can use it for the short POC SOW.

Ben
Ben Carter
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

- Peering CIDR (CardioSense side): 10.18.8.0/24
- Staging egress (public): 35.182.10.0/24 (as noted)

Acceptance criteria I filled into the spreadsheet: "VPC peering established; 50 successful smoke requests with <120ms median latency; keys rotated once after creation." I've signed the acceptance cell for scheduling Tues 2026-09-28 09:00–11:00 PDT. Security asked to receive the SOC2 scoping note and the field-level logging table before peering; Ben/Neha can you push that to security@cardiosense.ai?

Aisha
